title: Spain Lift Second World Cup Title as Ferran Torres Strikes in Extra Time to Deny Argentina
excerpt: A lone Ferran Torres goal in the 106th minute gave Spain a 1-0 victory over Argentina at New York New Jersey Stadium, sealing La Roja's first World Cup since 2010 and likely ending Lionel Messi's international career.
body:
• Spain beat Argentina 1-0 in extra time at New York New Jersey Stadium to win their second FIFA World Cup title, with Ferran Torres scoring in the 106th minute.
  • La Roja conceded just one goal across eight matches in the entire tournament, keeping six clean sheets and holding Argentina to zero shots on target in the final.
  • Enzo Fernández was sent off with a second yellow card in the 92nd minute, leaving Argentina to play extra time with 10 men as their bid for back-to-back World Cups fell short.
  • The victory, combined with the 2024 European Championship, positions Spain for a potential dynasty echoing their 2008-2012 triple-trophy era under a squad led by Rodri, Lamine Yamal, and Pedri.

Ferran Torres rifled a shot into the top of the net in the 106th minute to hand Spain their second FIFA World Cup title, denying Argentina a back-to-back championship and likely closing the book on Lionel Messi's extraordinary international career.

The match at the 80,663-capacity New York New Jersey Stadium in East Rutherford followed the script Spain had written across the entire tournament: suffocating defense, patient buildup, and a clinical finish when it mattered most. Through 90 minutes of regulation and the first half of extra time, neither side could break the deadlock, though Spain dominated possession at 64% and fired 12 shots to Argentina's solitary effort on target.

Torres Delivers the Decisive Blow

"Messi's first touch after kickoff didn't arrive until the 15th minute, and the seven-time Ballon d'Or winner managed just one shot across 120 minutes of play."

The breakthrough came in the 105th minute through a sequence of relentless Spanish pressure. Pedro Porro's cross found the head of Nico Williams on the far side of Argentina's box. Williams' pass found Torres — a 63rd-minute substitute for Mikel Oyarzabal — who slotted the ball past Emiliano Martínez into the top corner.

"For 2010 and Andrés Iniesta, now add 2026 and Torres."

— The Sun

Torres became only the fifth substitute to score in a World Cup final, and the first since Mario Götze sealed Germany's triumph against Argentina in 2014. He is also only the second Barcelona player to score a World Cup final winner, after Iniesta's iconic strike against the Netherlands in 2010.

Argentina's Toothless Attack and Fernández Red Card

Argentina were uncharacteristically subdued throughout. Messi's first touch after kickoff didn't arrive until the 15th minute, and the seven-time Ballon d'Or winner managed just one shot across 120 minutes of play. Emiliano Martínez kept his side alive with 10 saves — breaking the record of eight set by Brazil's Claudio Taffarel in the 1994 final — but received no attacking support.

Matters worsened for Argentina when midfielder Enzo Fernández collected a second yellow card in the 92nd minute for a reckless challenge on teenage defender Pau Cubarsí. Argentina played the entirety of extra time with 10 men, and their slim hopes of forcing a penalty shootout evaporated when Torres struck four minutes into the additional period.

Spain's Path to Glory

Luis de la Fuente's squad arrived in the final having conceded just one goal in seven previous matches. Their tournament campaign began with a scoreless draw against Cape Verde before comfortable wins over Saudi Arabia (4-0) and Uruguay (1-0) clinched Group H. In the knockout rounds, Spain dispatched Austria 3-0, edged Cristiano Ronaldo's Portugal 1-0, overcame Belgium 2-1 in the quarterfinals, and dominated France 2-0 in the semifinals.

Goalkeeper Unaí Simón, midfielder Rodri — who captained the side — and 19-year-old Lamine Yamal all delivered consistently strong performances. Mikel Oyarzabal finished the tournament with five goals, while the defensive partnership of Cubarsí and Aymeric Laporte proved virtually impenetrable.

End of an Era for Messi

The defeat almost certainly marks the end of Messi's international career. The 39-year-old Inter Miami star won the 2022 World Cup and two Copa América titles (2021, 2024) in a golden run, but could not rally his side in East Rutherford. He finished the 2026 tournament with eight goals and four assists — prolific numbers that ultimately counted for nothing in the final.

India's Football Fever

The final drew enormous viewership across India, where the sport's popularity has surged alongside the Indian Super League's growth. Maharashtra allowed restaurants to stay open until 4 AM for fans watching the early-morning broadcast. With India's football federation actively pursuing international hosting opportunities, Sunday's spectacle at MetLife only deepened the country's appetite for the world's biggest sporting event.
